A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SceneGenAgent research work, with readable text, figures, tables, mathematics, and complete Appendices A.1–A.6. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original industrial scene-generation experiments in Table 2, ablations in Table 3, data-scaling results in Figure 3, and an API-guidance experiment in Appendix A.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original benchmark, ablation, data-scaling, and appendix experimental results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same object retrieval, layout extraction, placement assignment and verification, C# code generation, and SceneInstruct fine-tuning procedures. The appendix prompts also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use SceneInstruct and the same 40 industrial scene descriptions across five evaluation categories. Appendix A.5 and Tables 5–7 retain every benchmark description.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains the same six open models plus GPT-4o and GLM-4-Plus. Comparator membership and configurations in Table 3 and Appendix A.1 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same training/validation split, model configurations, pass@1 metric, temperature of 1, and manual evaluation by three domain experts. Training settings in Table 4 and ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The agent and verification ablations in Table 3, training-data scaling analysis in Figure 3, and removal of API guidance in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. No robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report five generated samples per description in Section 4.1. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: All reported results match. Table 2 retains overall pass@1 of 81.0% for GPT-4o with SceneGenAgent and 78.5% for fine-tuned Llama3.1-70B; Table 3, Figure 3, and Appendix A.1 also retain their values and findings.

T1.justification: The scene, placement, position, relation, and coordinate-difference definitions in Sections 2–3 are unchanged, as are the geometric constraints. Text moving between pages 2 and 3 does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: precise industrial scene generation through SceneGenAgent, construction of SceneInstruct, and improved open-model performance approaching GPT-4o.

C2.justification: Interpretations of layout verification, data scaling, and API guidance are identical. The limitations concerning industrial-domain coverage and labor-intensive, potentially subjective manual evaluation are also retained.

D1.justification: Appendices A.2–A.4 retain the same data-construction details, training hyperparameters, prompts, and code templates. Code/data access statements and embedded external link targets are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5, citations, and references are unchanged. The positioning of SceneGenAgent relative to prior scene-generation and layout-refinement methods remains identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds asterisks to Xiao Xia and Dan Zhang and an 'Equal contribution' footnote, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The new authorship footnote causes limited text reflow and changed column/page breaks on pages 1–3. Figures 1–3 and Tables 1–7 are unchanged; pages 4–21 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies equal authorship and updates version metadata, with minor layout reflow. The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
